**Summary of analysis:**

**Test image key features:**
- Large, irregular brown/tan necrotic patches spanning much of the leaf area
- Lesions originate from leaf margins and tips, spreading inward
- Grayish-white area visible near midrib/central stem junction - suggests possible sporulation or mycelial growth
- Multiple leaves affected with dark/brown stems visible in background
- No concentric ring pattern (rules out Early Blight)
- No small discrete spots (rules out Septoria Leaf Blotch or Bacterial Speck)

**Differential reasoning:**
- **Late Blight** (top candidate): Large irregular water-soaked to brown/black lesions starting at margins, with possible grayish-white sporulation (Phytophthora sporangiophores) at lesion edges — classic presentation
- **Gray Mold**: Also causes large tan-brown necrotic areas with gray fluffy sporulation, but typically more obviously gray/fuzzy
- **Early Blight**: Shows concentric rings in discrete spots — not seen here
- The grayish-white zone near the midrib is subtle but consistent with the white downy sporulation that Late Blight produces under humid conditions

The pattern of large, rapidly-spreading dark irregular necrotic lesions with grayish margins, progressing from leaf edges across entire leaflets, is most characteristic of Late Blight.
